headline: High-risk shared filesystem and MCP-based orchestration create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure between ms-swift and Semantic Kernel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift reads/writes files and consumes stdin/stdout, while Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and plugins. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred from documented capabilities, not directly reproduced, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ms-swift outputs untrusted text into files or stdout that Semantic Kernel later parses as instructions
IF Semantic Kernel connects to an MCP server or plugin that forwards ms-swift-generated content without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict provenance tag to all cross-agent messages
Route inter-agent text through a schema validator
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported files
Review MCP/plugin inputs before execution
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces and trust boundaries

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets, and Semantic Kernel can read/write application-defined files while using broad network egress and plugin credentials. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive artifacts from ms-swift can flow into Semantic Kernel outputs or third-party APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or memory store
IF Semantic Kernel forwards imported files or context to an external model provider or plugin
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Redact secrets before handoff
Disable file ingestion for sensitive directories
Audit outbound plugin/API destinations
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and read files, and Semantic Kernel explicitly supports multiple instances with shared state via a memory store. ms-swift also runs shell commands and subprocesses, increasing the chance of concurrent mutation if both target the same resources. No locking is documented, so overlapping writes are a realistic default-risk conflict.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or shared memory store
IF ms-swift shell actions and Semantic Kernel plugin actions target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Turn off shared memory for concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs, and ms-swift can generate model outputs, logs, and evaluation artifacts that may be consumed downstream. If Semantic Kernel treats ms-swift output as authoritative, errors can cascade into external actions or incorrect agent behavior. Because the profiles do not show a verification gate, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses ms-swift output as input to a plugin or tool call without validation
IF downstream plugins can send emails, modify records, or call external APIs
mitigations: Insert a human review step before tool execution
Validate ms-swift outputs against a schema
Require citations or source links for factual claims
Log and diff tool inputs before action
requires-engineering: add policy checks before plugin invocation

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, datasets, checkpoints, and logs, while Semantic Kernel handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through Semantic Kernel plugins or external model providers, retention and jurisdiction can diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ms-swift datasets or logs and then forwarded through Semantic Kernel plugins
IF the chosen model provider or plugin stores data outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Block regulated data from external plugins
Use region-locked providers only
Set short retention on logs and traces
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
